Subject: Follow-up: HIPAA / BAA questions + next steps

Hi Rajiv - great to meet you and the HealthCloud team earlier. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps re: HIPAA/PHI handling:

1) Questions we captured from your side:
- Do you support a BAA? Which deployment modes are eligible?
- Is PHI ever stored or persisted by Redwood? What controls exist around logging/telemetry?
- SOC 2 status and how to get the report (NDA?).
- KMS/HSM support for customer keys and encryption-at-rest.

2) Short answers (high level):
- BAA: Redwood offers a BAA for Dedicated (reserved capacity) and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. Our public Hosted API is not eligible for BAA or PHI processing by default.
- PHI: PHI processing is supported in Dedicated and Private modes with contractual controls. Customers can choose to disable persistent telemetry and enable audit logging only to customer-managed stores.
- SOC 2: Redwood maintains a SOC 2 Type II report; we can share the report under NDA.
- KMS: We support customer-managed keys (KMS) for Private/Dedicated.

Attachments: I'm attaching our initial security questionnaire (Redwood_Security_Questionnaire_v1.pdf) and a short note on obtaining the SOC 2 report (Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_NDA_instructions.txt). Also linking the BAA template for legal review (DocuSign link will be provided once legal confirms).

Next steps I propose:
- Dev/Infra deep-dive to confirm architecture and encryption settings (Dev, are you available Wed or Thu?)
- HealthCloud legal to review the BAA template - I can route via DocuSign if you prefer.
- We can run a short technical checklist (15-30m) to confirm PHI flows and any redaction/de-identification needs.

Would you be available for a 30-minute follow-up with your infra and legal on Thu 7/24 at 10:00am PT?

Thanks - I'll leave Dev on to answer the deeper infra questions.

Hi Rajiv - quick technical responses to your items below. Happy to walk through these on the call.

1) Hosted API eligibility:
- Correct: Redwood's public Hosted API is not approved for PHI ingestion or processing. There is no contractual BAA option for the public Hosted API. Customers requiring PHI must use Dedicated (reserved capacity) or Private (VPC/on-prem).

2) BAA & SLA:
- BAA: We have a standard BAA template (attached: Redwood_BAA_Template.docx).
- SLA: Dedicated customers can opt into a higher SLA (99.9% uptime) and defined escalation paths; BAA customers typically choose Dedicated or Private with our enterprise support add-on. Specific SLA addenda can be negotiated in the contract.

3) Data persistence and logging:
- By default, in Hosted we collect request telemetry and short-term logs to monitor performance and detect abuse; this is not suitable for PHI.
- For Dedicated and Private, we offer a configuration that disables persistent request logging and telemetry ingestion for customer payloads. In that configuration:
  - Prompt text and model outputs are not written to long-term analytics stores owned by Redwood.
  - Short-lived KV cache is kept in-memory and can be configured to evict immediately after response.
  - Audit logs (access, config changes, infra events) can be exported to customer-managed logging (e.g., CloudWatch / Stackdriver / S3) and are under the customer's control.
- Items that could contain PHI if enabled: prompt text, response text, custom metadata fields. We recommend treating any free-text fields as PHI unless explicitly de-identified.

4) KMS / encryption:
- We support AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and GCP KMS for customer-managed keys on Dedicated and Private deployments. For Private on-prem, customers may bring HSMs or KMS endpoints.
- Data at rest for model inputs/outputs and KV caches can be encrypted with customer keys in these modes.

5) Operational controls / evidence:
- SOC 2 Type II report available under NDA (instructions attached).
- We can provide architecture diagrams, pen-test summaries, and a temporary Jira link for deeper evidence (JIRA-SUP-1245).

Attachments: Redwood_BAA_Template.docx (BAA standard), Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_NDA_instructions.txt (how to request SOC2).

Suggested next steps:
- Legal review of BAA (we can route via DocuSign)
- 45m infra deep-dive to confirm KMS setup and logging/export configuration - propose Thu 7/24 10:00am PT as Marissa proposed.

If you want, I can include a short checklist for your infra team to complete before the call (KMS region, VPC peering, allowed egress).

Thanks - Dev
